newsitem.title: UK: Turkey's planned dollar bond seen at low 300 b.p..
newsitem.headline: Turkey's planned dollar bond seen at low 300 b.p..

text.p: Turkey's planned 10-year dollar bond is expected to be launched in the low 300 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, bankers said on Monday.
"The bid that won this mandate is in the low 300s. If the bond is launched at less than 300 it won't work," a syndicate manager, away from the lead managers, said.
A trade magazine said the deal could be priced in a range of 320-340 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes.
In May, Turkey launched a $400 million five-year bond to yield 350 b.p. over the 6.625 percent April 2002 U.S. Treasury.
That bond had last tightened to trade at around 270 b.p. over, dealers said.
Turkey on Monday mandated Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers to lead its Eurodollar issue, expected to be set in September, the Turkish treasury said.
Bankers expect the size of the bond to be around $400-500 million with a maturity of around 10 years.
Turkey had also considered the mark sector.
Turkey has raised around $1.4 billion in the international capital markets so far this year.
It last issued a 1.0 billion mark five-year bond in early June.
The republic also launched a seven-year 500 million mark issue in January, a five-year 300 billion lire deal in February and the above mentioned five-year $400 million bond in May.
"Turkey will continue to borrow in line with its target of extending maturity and lowering borrowing costs," the treasury said.
